procedures.name: Tree Landing
procedures.trigger_condition_text: Emergency landing in a forested area

trigger_condition.description: Emergency landing in a forested area

aircraft_state.description: Emergency landing in a forested area

evidence.source_excerpt: Although a tree landing is not an attractive prospect, the following general guidelines help to make the experience survivable.

source_evidence.source_excerpt: Although a tree landing is not an attractive prospect, the following general guidelines help to make the experience survivable.

steps.action: Use the normal landing configuration (full flaps, gear down)
steps.expected_result: Aircraft is configured for landing

evidence.source_excerpt: Use the normal landing configuration (full flaps, gear down).

steps.action: Head into the wind to keep groundspeed low
steps.expected_result: Reduced groundspeed upon landing

evidence.source_excerpt: Keep the groundspeed low by heading into the wind.

steps.action: Make contact at minimum indicated airspeed, but not below stall speed
steps.expected_result: Controlled landing attitude in tree branches

evidence.source_excerpt: Make contact at minimum indicated airspeed, but not below stall speed, and 'hang' the airplane in the tree branches in a nose-high landing attitude.

steps.action: Involve the underside of the fuselage and both wings in the initial tree contact
steps.expected_result: More even and positive cushioning effect

evidence.source_excerpt: Involving the underside of the fuselage and both wings in the initial tree contact provides a more even and positive cushioning effect.

steps.action: Avoid direct contact of the fuselage with heavy tree trunks
steps.expected_result: Minimized risk of damage to the fuselage

evidence.source_excerpt: Avoid direct contact of the fuselage with heavy tree trunks.

steps.action: Aim for low, closely spaced trees with wide, dense crowns
steps.expected_result: Safer landing environment

evidence.source_excerpt: Low, closely spaced trees with wide, dense crowns (branches) close to the ground are much better than tall trees with thin tops.

steps.action: Ensure initial tree contact is symmetrical
steps.expected_result: Maintained proper airplane attitude

evidence.source_excerpt: Ideally, initial tree contact should be symmetrical; that is, both wings should meet equal resistance in the tree branches.

steps.action: Direct the airplane between two properly spaced trees if heavy trunk contact is unavoidable
steps.expected_result: Simultaneous wing contact to minimize damage

evidence.source_excerpt: If heavy tree trunk contact is unavoidable once the airplane is on the ground, it is best to involve both wings simultaneously by directing the airplane between two properly spaced trees.

procedures.name: Emergency Descent
procedures.trigger_condition_text: Uncontrollable fire, sudden loss of cabin pressurization, or any situation demanding an immediate and rapid descent

trigger_condition.description: Uncontrollable fire, sudden loss of cabin pressurization, or any situation demanding an immediate and rapid descent

aircraft_state.description: Uncontrollable fire, sudden loss of cabin pressurization, or any situation demanding an immediate and rapid descent

evidence.source_excerpt: An emergency descent is a maneuver for descending as rapidly as possible to a lower altitude or to the ground for an emergency landing.

source_evidence.source_excerpt: An emergency descent is a maneuver for descending as rapidly as possible to a lower altitude or to the ground for an emergency landing.

steps.action: Establish a bank of approximately 30 to 45°
steps.expected_result: Maintain positive load factors (G forces) on the airplane

evidence.source_excerpt: When initiating the descent, a bank of approximately 30 to 45° should be established to maintain positive load factors (G forces) on the airplane.

steps.action: Reduce power to idle
steps.expected_result: Allow the propeller to act as an aerodynamic brake

evidence.source_excerpt: Except when prohibited by the manufacturer, the power should be reduced to idle, and the propeller control (if equipped) should be placed in the low pitch (or high revolutions per minute (rpm)) position.

steps.action: Extend landing gear and flaps as recommended by the manufacturer
steps.expected_result: Provide maximum drag for rapid descent without excessive airspeed

evidence.source_excerpt: The landing gear and flaps should be extended as recommended by the manufacturer. This provides maximum drag so that the descent can be made as rapidly as possible, without excessive airspeed.

steps.action: Ensure airspeed does not exceed never-exceed speed, maximum landing gear extended speed, or maximum flap extended speed
steps.expected_result: Prevent structural damage to the airplane

evidence.source_excerpt: The pilot should not allow the airplane’s airspeed to pass the never-exceed speed (V NE), the maximum landing gear extended speed (V LE), or the maximum flap extended speed (V FE), as applicable.

steps.action: Comply with design maneuvering speed (V A) limitations if in turbulent conditions
steps.expected_result: Ensure safe descent without structural stress

evidence.source_excerpt: If the descent is conducted in turbulent conditions, the pilot also needs to comply with the design maneuvering speed (V A) limitations.

steps.action: Initiate recovery from the emergency descent at a high enough altitude
steps.expected_result: Ensure a safe recovery back to level flight or a precautionary landing

evidence.source_excerpt: The recovery from an emergency descent should be initiated at a high enough altitude to ensure a safe recovery back to level flight or a precautionary landing.

warnings.description: Prolonged practice of emergency descents should be avoided to prevent excessive cooling of the engine cylinders.

steps.expected_result: Retain the ability to communicate and navigate

The first steps necessary for surviving an encounter with IMC by a VFR pilot are as follows: Recognition and acceptance of the seriousness of the situation and the need for immediate remedial action; Maintaining control of the airplane; Obtaining the appropriate assistance to get the airplane safely on the ground.

source_evidence.source_excerpt: The first steps necessary for surviving an encounter with IMC by a VFR pilot are as follows: Recognition and acceptance of the seriousness of the situation and the need for immediate remedial action; Maintaining control of the airplane; Obtaining the appropriate assistance to get the airplane safely on the ground.

steps.action: Recognize and accept the seriousness of the situation and the need for immediate remedial action
steps.expected_result: Pilot acknowledges the emergency and prepares to take control measures.

evidence.source_excerpt: Recognition and acceptance of the seriousness of the situation and the need for immediate remedial action.

steps.action: Maintain control of the airplane using flight instruments
steps.expected_result: Pilot keeps the airplane under control without relying on visual references.

evidence.source_excerpt: The only way to control the airplane safely is by using and trusting the flight instruments.

steps.action: Keep the wings level
steps.expected_result: Prevents uncontrolled turns and maintains stability.

evidence.source_excerpt: The most important concern—in fact the only concern at this point—is to keep the wings level.

steps.action: Trim the airplane to maintain hands-off level flight
steps.expected_result: Reduces pilot workload and helps maintain control.

evidence.source_excerpt: Trim the airplane with the elevator trim so that it maintains hands-off level flight at cruise airspeed.

steps.action: Make all attitude changes smooth and small
steps.expected_result: Minimizes the risk of over-controlling the airplane.

evidence.source_excerpt: Make all attitude changes smooth and small, yet with positive pressure.

steps.action: Avoid combined maneuvers such as climbing or descending turns
steps.expected_result: Reduces the risk of control loss.

evidence.source_excerpt: Combined maneuvers, such as climbing or descending turns, should be avoided if at all possible by an untrained instrument pilot.

steps.action: Request ATC assistance if necessary
steps.expected_result: Ensures safe landing and guidance.

evidence.source_excerpt: It's reasonable to ask the controller to slow down, if this becomes an issue.

steps.action: Transition to visual flight when conditions allow
steps.expected_result: Pilot safely lands the aircraft.

evidence.source_excerpt: The pilot should take this into account and, if possible, allow time to become acclimatized and geographically oriented before attempting an approach and landing.
